title: Audit of the reacting-thermals SIMDE claim: I, D, S replicate at dt/2 and 1.5x grid; E and M hold by construction (a non-burning, heat-conserving thermal rises at the caps' speed: the motion is buoyant drift in imposed gravity)
summary: Construction: read world.py; no body, division or death rule; heat is build-from-food with decay (E by construction) and the only force moving a body is the imposed uniform gravity acting on the body field (g dT/dx). Deciding control for M: switching burning off and heat loss off at t=300 on seed 32 leaves the caps rising at the fed caps' speed (0.48 vs 0.41 px/t) with the same mushroom shape until they smear out in ~25 t, so the motion is passive buoyant rise and burning only keeps the body alive. Replication on fresh seeds: seed 32 (23 persistent splits, generation 7, 8 of 10 dividing caps travel 3 sqrt(area)), world dt/2 seed 33 (34, gen 6, 8 of 16), true 1.5x grid seed 34 (65, gen 7, 43 of 58); seed 31 goes extinct in the initial burn-out (1 of 16 fresh seeds), 12 of 12 screen seeds survive to t=200. Fuel fork on seed 32: 20 -> 0 bodies in 2 t.

verdicts.limitation: M: the passive-thermal arm changes two terms at once (no burning, no heat loss) to keep the heat; it shows the speed comes from buoyancy of hot fluid, not from the burning. Whether buoyant rise in a uniform imposed gravity counts as self-propulsion is a rubric judgement: I read L4b's 'no imposed field' as excluding it, as sedimentation would be. Dividing-cap counts at 3 body lengths, if M were scored: 8 of 10, 8 of 16, 43 of 58 (sqrt area); 5 of 10, 2 of 16, 19 of 58 (long axis). 1 of 16 fresh seeds went extinct, so S is likely but not certain. Single seeds per numerical variant.
